questionText: Consider three machines M, N, and P with IP addresses 100.10.5.2, 100.10.5.5, and 100.10.5.6 respectively. The subnet mask is set to 255.255.255.252 for all the three machines. Which one of the following is true?
options: M, N, and P all belong to the same subnet
Only M and N belong to the same subnet
Only N and P belong to the same subnet
M, N, and P belong to three different subnets
explanation:
To determine which machines belong to the same subnet, perform a bitwise AND operation between each IP address and the subnet mask $255.255.255.252$.

Subnet Mask Analysis:
The last octet of the subnet mask is $252 = 11111100_2$.
The block size is $256 - 252 = 4$.
Thus, the subnet boundaries in the last octet occur in multiples of $4$ ($0, 4, 8, \dots$).

Network ID Calculation:
1. Machine M ($100.10.5.2$):
Last octet is $2$. $2 \text{ AND } 252 = 0$.
Network ID = $100.10.5.0$

2. Machine N ($100.10.5.5$):
Last octet is $5$. $5 \text{ AND } 252 = 4$.
Network ID = $100.10.5.4$

3. Machine P ($100.10.5.6$):
Last octet is $6$. $6 \text{ AND } 252 = 4$.
Network ID = $100.10.5.4$

Conclusion:
Machine N and Machine P share the same Network ID ($100.10.5.4$), whereas Machine M has a different Network ID ($100.10.5.0$). Hence, only N and P belong to the same subnet.
